preexecution_amendment: Removed the redundant active-state observe_goal wrapper before any model execution; the clean replay's trusted goal result is the sole certification trigger.
research_role: mechanism qualification on already consumed design cases; not a held-out effect estimate

mechanisms: same-session candidate compilation at first believed feasibility
incumbent fallback on provider or safety-cap termination
treatment.state_retained: canonical bootstrap program, certificate, and trajectory metadata only

algorithm_invariants: A-F and B-FSR runner identities and prompts remain unchanged
construction-state success alone never becomes a final submission
only a clean-replay-passed canonical program can become the incumbent
a later program replaces the incumbent only after its own clean replay passes
provider failure and request or wall-clock safety caps may select the latest incumbent without another model decision
no official evaluator result is visible before generation terminates
no cross-case package cache, case-specific package rule, or container filesystem checkpoint is used

case_selection.reason: pair03 exposed a live-state to reproducible-program gap that clean replay repaired
pair07 exposed a long post-feasibility tail and ad hoc self-managed replay
pair08 exposed the distinction between early benchmark feasibility and later runtime-quality work

qualification_questions: Does the Agent clean-replay a complete program as soon as it believes the full goal is feasible?
Does every stored incumbent hash have a matching clean-replay certificate?
Does final generation preserve a certified program even when the Agent continues quality work?
Does the submitted or fallback program pass the EnvBench Official evaluator?
How do requests, tokens, shell work, replay time, and post-goal tail compare descriptively with the frozen A-F and B-FSR trajectories?

implementation: all incumbent updates are certificate-backed and hash-consistent
the selected final script is certified
no tracked repository or evaluator mutation is accepted
fallback behavior is covered by deterministic tests even if no live provider interruption occurs
mechanism: at least one episode obtains a clean-replay Pass and stores an incumbent
every clean-replay Pass either stores a hash-matched incumbent or records why the certificate was rejected
Official outcomes and deployment-quality diagnostics are reported separately
not_a_requirement: lower resource use on every case
higher success rate on this selected three-case batch

stopping_and_change_policy.on_implementation_defect: stop, mark affected episodes invalid, fix under a new code hash, and preregister a replacement qualification
stopping_and_change_policy.after_batch: adjudicate mechanism behavior before touching the remaining eight unrun Dev16 cases
